correctness.rationale: The Haar basis is orthonormal. Ancestor-closed masks span precisely contiguous dyadic-block constants, and the averaging projector contracts path variation by decomposition into unit steps; nonempty such masks attain norm one at a leaf boundary. If a retained interval has an unretained parent, a step at its midpoint has projection values c-1/2, c+1/2 on its halves and c on the sibling, after any selected ancestor contributions; the two distinct neighboring differences sum to 3/2. A single root-child coefficient has exact induced norm (3/sqrt(L))*(sqrt(L)/2)=3/2. The standalone exact-integer checker exhaustively confirms masks through depth four, but the proof is valid for all depths independently of those finite computations.

value.rationale: For every finite Haar resolution and every retained-detail mask, the theorem gives a complete exact combinatorial TVD criterion plus a uniform, attained 50% instability separation when it fails. Dyadic tree selection is a standard natural signal-reconstruction constraint, and the gap is a concrete variation design cost absent from mere Euclidean orthogonality. It identifies precisely when arbitrary wavelet coefficient deletion can introduce noncontractive path oscillation, not an artificial finite table.
